authorship: Generated from the production Rust catalogue; not model output or expert qualification

contracts.title: Relationship, marriage and feelings
contracts.roles: Prospective partner is seventh even if no partner is named. Use operative capacity for a specific person's feelings (e.g. neighbour: third). House rulers have priority; never infer gender or allocate Sun/Venus by a name.
contracts.judgment: Distinguish hoped-for formation, current feelings and an arranged wedding. An unnamed prospective partner is a role: do not claim an existing person currently loves the querent or has already met them. Directed reception describes chart testimony; event perfection is a separate question. No contact is not an automatic cancellation of an arranged wedding.

contracts.title: Lost inanimate possession
contracts.roles: Own lost object: compare Lords 2 and 4 with its supplied description. Someone else's: owner's turned second only. Prefer one justified main ruler; Moon is secondary only with a reason.
contracts.judgment: Consider recovery before proposing a search. Angularity and clear whereabouts can support recovery without an applying aspect. Keep search reports fallible; no thief unless raised. A failed search revisits this chart.

contracts.title: Lost animal
contracts.roles: Kind determines sixth (dog/cat) versus twelfth (horse), not measured size. Do not turn every animal from its owner: the neighbour's cat example uses the ordinary sixth.
contracts.judgment: Assess recovery and plausible whereabouts from supplied context, without exact GPS promises or automatic void-Moon rejection.

contracts.title: Missing person
contracts.roles: Use the person's actual operative relationship, not the movable-object recipe or an automatic seventh for every missing person.
contracts.judgment: Consider recovery/contact and location separately. Retain reported circumstances as reports.

contracts.title: Sale or purchase of movable goods
contracts.roles: Transaction action and requested outcome are separate. For pure completion, use the actual contracting parties without demanding title ownership or an asset-condition role. An unspecified counterparty is the deal actor's seventh; an identified relative keeps their own operative house. For quality/profit, goods sold are the relevant owner's second; a buyer's potential goods are the buyer's second. Title owner, contracting party and intermediary are distinct.
contracts.judgment: Preserve deal, quality or profit as asked. Non-property opposition may complete with regret. This recipe provides no exact count of books/tulips sold. A venue/date is event context, never the chart anchor.

contracts.title: Payment, debt, gift or grant
contracts.roles: Customers/spouse: eighth; job or government money: eleventh; known relative's money: their turned second. Preserve entitlement versus discretionary gift. For arrival, retain the recipient's own role and second-house pocket, plus Moon when the recipient is the effective principal and a house ruler does not already claim Moon (p. 158).
contracts.judgment: Arrival considers money contacting the recipient, their pocket, or the appropriate Moon; an absent direct money/Lord 1 contact cannot discard the other routes. Amount/quality does not universally require an arrival aspect. Do not turn signs/degrees into an invented exact currency amount.

contracts.title: Shares and investments
contracts.roles: Owned shares are the principal's second-house possessions, not automatically eighth-house money.
contracts.judgment: Judge condition/value and scope. Do not promise an exact return or treat this as a payment-arrival question.

contracts.title: Getting a new external job
contracts.roles: Principal's own house and radical tenth for the external job, even for a third-party principal. If the person is themselves tenth-house, use their turned tenth. Wages are a separate role.
contracts.judgment: Establish getting the job, not merely contacting wages. An explicitly mentioned intermediary may matter; do not invent one.

contracts.title: Keeping a job or existing career
contracts.roles: Current job/career/boss uses the relevant person's turned tenth. Distinguish co-worker seventh and subordinate sixth.
contracts.judgment: Default is an existing job: assess stability/disruption, not a compulsory acquisition aspect.

contracts.title: Returning to an old job
contracts.roles: Principal and relevant job; keep the old-job re-entry context.
contracts.judgment: Use re-entry testimony, not the generic get/keep assumption. State limitations of contact coverage.

contracts.title: Assessing an available job
contracts.roles: The external job is radical tenth, except a tenth-house worker uses their turned tenth (seventh). Select job.wages when assessing pay: second from the bound job, normally eleventh, or eighth in that exception. Job, wages and worker's pocket are distinct roles (printed pp. 223–227). An offer already available is not a new acquisition.
contracts.judgment: Judge quality and stated priorities using their relevant roles. A pay priority needs wages testimony; a wages aspect does not prove job acquisition. Ask priorities only if the answer truly depends on what 'good' means.

contracts.title: Boss, colleague or subordinate
contracts.roles: Co-worker seventh, subordinate sixth, boss tenth when directly asked about. Job/boss collisions need a justified contextual allocation.
contracts.judgment: Address the actual work relationship; do not reclassify a friendly colleague as eleventh by habit.

contracts.title: Buying or selling property
contracts.roles: Ordinary actual contracting parties are first/seventh; a specific relative may take their own house. A routine estate agent is not the contracting seller and does not acquire a turned seventh by handling the sale. Pure completion does not require deed ownership. For asset assessment, property fourth and price tenth in the relevant frame; the buyer's prospective interest is not current title. Profit is distinct.
contracts.judgment: Assess condition, price and completion separately. Opposition may complete a sale; don't apply this exception to an ongoing rental.

contracts.title: Rental agreement
contracts.roles: Modern tenant/landlord deal: first/seventh, not an automatic sixth-house servant.
contracts.judgment: An opposition can imply regret in this ongoing relationship. Distinguish an available tenancy's quality from finding one.

contracts.title: Property used for business
contracts.roles: Property to work on/in uses the book's business/property-profit distinction, not an indiscriminate ordinary home-price allocation.
contracts.judgment: Dedicated profit testimony and reviewed role allocation are required before this program can deliver a judgment.

contracts.title: Stay, change or compare alternatives
contracts.roles: General stay/change: first is things as they are, seventh the changed situation. Specific work versus college can use the relevant houses. Current home versus homeland is conditional context.
contracts.judgment: Do not mechanically place Lord 1 in seventh. A finite shortlist and meaningful comparison must remain visible.

contracts.title: Hiring staff
contracts.roles: Employee sixth. Candidate descriptions support a reviewed matching decision, not arbitrary planets.
contracts.judgment: Availability is assumed in this recipe; no obligatory acquisition aspect. Dedicated candidate-matching program awaits review.

contracts.title: Contact with someone
contracts.roles: The person takes their operative relationship house.
contracts.judgment: Contact with the person differs from the arrival of their parcel. An expected contact and long-lost return have different defaults.

contracts.title: Arrival of a letter or parcel
contracts.roles: Before receipt, the parcel is the sender's relevant possession; afterwards it is the receiver's.
contracts.judgment: An aspect to the seller alone does not show arrival of the parcel. Dedicated sender/parcel program needs review.

contracts.title: Expected visit
contracts.roles: Visitor's capacity matters: plumber is not a friend. Establish whether the visit is actually expected.
contracts.judgment: Use the naturally limited contextual scale. Do not request birth data or full street address by habit.

contracts.title: Sporting match or championship
contracts.roles: Us/them depends on actual allegiance, not home/away or name order. Moon is not automatically the ordinary querent co-significator.
contracts.judgment: Match versus season/championship differs. An indifferent spectator has no invented allegiance. Dedicated contest program awaits review.

contracts.title: Profit from a bet
contracts.roles: Money/profit question, not the team's us/them match recipe.
contracts.judgment: Assess the principal's money and relevant gains without promising an exact payout.

contracts.title: Civil trial or legal dispute
contracts.roles: Parties first/seventh, legal process tenth, verdict fourth. A lawyer can relay the client's genuine question.
contracts.judgment: Dedicated trial/perfection program awaits review; identify the actual party and issue without inferring a legal outcome from a generic deal.

contracts.title: Vehicle or journey safety
contracts.roles: Ship I sail in is first in that capacity; movable possession is second. Presence aboard is not a prerequisite.
contracts.judgment: Dedicated safety judgment requires review; identify the undertaking without replacing the question time with departure time.

contracts.title: Description of a person
contracts.roles: An identified person uses kind=person and owner_id=their actual ID; their operative relationship fixes their ruler. An explicitly unnamed future marriage partner uses kind=person_role, name=Future marriage partner, and owner_id=the role's principal (querent or an identified participant). Derive that principal's seventh; never invent a spouse identity.
contracts.judgment: Broad comparative description, not exact height, ethnicity or invented marks. Use the main significator, not a natural cosignificator. Dedicated descriptive program needs review.

contracts.title: Whether information is true
contracts.roles: A substantive relationship/job/etc. question normally uses its underlying matter; superficial 'is it true' wording is not a new universal recipe.
contracts.judgment: Preserve the specific reported claim. Dedicated veracity program awaits review.

contracts.title: Trustworthiness in a capacity
contracts.roles: Judge the relevant person's condition, not a generic message-veracity house.
contracts.judgment: State the capacity and the actual concern; avoid accusations unsupported by the reading.

contracts.title: Current pregnancy
contracts.roles: Current state differs from future conception. Turning follows the principal and parenthood context; never infer paternity from a name.
contracts.judgment: Dedicated pregnancy/medical qualification is required; the chart is not a clinical test.

contracts.title: Conception and fertility
contracts.roles: Conception, carrying to term and lifetime potential are different scopes; relevant parent roles need explicit facts.
contracts.judgment: The source's coarse childbirth count is specific to this recipe, not transferable to sales. Dedicated program awaits review.

contracts.title: Adoption
contracts.roles: Prospective adoption is someone else's child; a completed adoption is one's own fifth-house child.
contracts.judgment: Do not erase adoption state. Dedicated role/testimony program awaits review.

contracts.title: Illness or treatment
contracts.roles: Patient/capacity, diagnosis/prognosis/treatment differ. Lord 6 is not automatically the illness.
contracts.judgment: The textbook's medical overview is not complete diagnosis training. Dedicated clinical-scope and judgment qualification is required.

contracts.title: Political election
contracts.roles: Incumbent/open contest and supporter/impartial citizen/foreign observer change assignment. Citizenship is not inferred from device location.
contracts.judgment: Dedicated election program awaits review; preserve candidates and actual observer capacity.

contracts.title: Knowledge and its earnings
contracts.roles: Knowledge ninth, profit tenth; employed job tenth/wages eleventh is different.
contracts.judgment: Profit already arising from knowledge does not universally need an arrival aspect. Dedicated program awaits review.

contracts.title: Examination
contracts.roles: Exam result/profit from knowledge is not just a ninth-house object.
contracts.judgment: Admission and passing can differ; preserve which was asked. Dedicated program awaits review.

contracts.title: Voyage, course or fair benefit
contracts.roles: Undertaking quality differs from its profit; don't blindly reuse movable-goods sale roles.
contracts.judgment: Identify the actual benefit asked about. Dedicated program awaits review.

contracts.title: Dream meaning or prophetic truth
contracts.roles: Dream meaning uses contextual ordinary roles; prophetic truth has its own ninth-house distinction.
contracts.judgment: Chart the question's time, not the dream's time. Dedicated interpretation program awaits review.

contracts.title: School or university
contracts.roles: Institution radical third/ninth, not blindly turned from a child.
contracts.judgment: Admission, enjoyment and quality are distinct. Dedicated education program awaits review.

contracts.title: An unspecified wish
contracts.roles: Specific matters use their own method; not every wish is eleventh.
contracts.judgment: Ask what the concern is without demanding disclosure. No invented judgment for an unspecified wish.

contracts.title: Tax and assessment
contracts.roles: Government tenth, its coffers eleventh, principal's money second.
contracts.judgment: Amount/assessment and ability to bear it differ. No fabricated exact tax amount; dedicated program awaits review.

contracts.title: Reported harmful practice
contracts.roles: Keep allegations as reported concerns. Special relationships matter only when supplied.
contracts.judgment: A future applying aspect cannot prove a past act. No unprompted accusation; dedicated program awaits review.

contracts.title: Imprisonment or release
contracts.roles: Whether already in custody is indispensable. Relevant radical and turned twelfth need explicit consideration.
contracts.judgment: Entry and release have different defaults; dedicated program awaits review.

contracts.title: Weather in a place or at an event
contracts.roles: Target locality/season and event's house are context, not chart coordinates or question time.
contracts.judgment: Dedicated weather program awaits review; do not treat this as a forecast from meteorological observations.

contracts.title: Choosing when to act by horary
contracts.roles: Horary election works from the original question chart, not a new future chart or a full natal election.
contracts.judgment: Feasible action window and real constraints matter. Native exact-perfection timing is currently insufficient; dedicated program awaits review.

contracts.title: Matter not yet identified
contracts.roles: Do not guess the subject or force it into a familiar house.
contracts.judgment: Elicit the actual concern; retain ambiguity until a method can be selected.

fields.question: Are you asking for yourself, about someone else, or passing on their own question?
Whose own question are you passing on?
What circumstance do I need to understand about this question?
Where are you asking from? A city and country will do; the event's venue is separate.
What date and local time did you understand this earlier question?
That clock time happened twice. Do you mean the earlier occurrence or the later one?
Where is the event taking place?
When is that event taking place?
What time span does your question concern?
Is this about a hoped-for relationship, one already under way, or an arranged wedding?
What does the missing object look like—its colour, material or shape?
What kind of animal is missing?
What concern about theft have you already raised?
What happened when you searched the suggested place?
Are you buying, selling or renting?
Whose purchase, sale or rental agreement are we considering?
Whose financial benefit are you asking about?
Who is the other party in this particular deal?
Who is selling the goods? That may be different from who owns them.
Where is the money coming from—a customer, job, government, or someone you know?
Is this money already owed to you, or a gift or grant they can choose to give?
Is this a new job, your current job, a return, or an offer you can already take?
Is this person your boss, a colleague, or someone who works for you?
What would make this option good for you in this question?
What would staying with things as they are mean?
What are the alternatives you are comparing?
By home, do you mean your current home or your homeland?
Who are the candidates you could hire? A brief description of each will do.
Who is sending the parcel, and in what capacity?
Who is coming to visit, and who are they to you?
Is this visit already expected, or are you hoping they will come?
Which side do you support, or are you asking about a bet's profit?
Is this about one match, a season, or a championship?
What specific claim or concern would you like me to consider?
Whose parenthood is involved in this question?
Are you asking about conceiving soon, carrying a pregnancy, or ever having children?
Is this adoption still prospective, or is the child already yours?
Who is the child's birth parent to you?
Is your question about the illness, its course, or a particular treatment?
Which treatment or treatments are you asking about?
Are you supporting a candidate, an impartial citizen, or an observer from elsewhere?
Is there an incumbent standing again, or is this an open contest?
Which office and election are you asking about?
Are you asking about the knowledge itself, or earnings from using it?
Are you asking about passing this exam, or being admitted?
Would you like to explore the dream's meaning, or whether it foretells something?
What happened in the dream?
Is this a school or a university?
Are you asking about admission, enjoyment, or the quality of the education?
Is this person already in custody, or are you asking whether they will be?
Is this about the weather generally, or at a particular event?
Where is the weather you are asking about? This is separate from where we cast the question.
What day or season is this weather question about?
What action would you like to find a time for?
What dates or time window are actually available for that action?
What real constraints affect when you can act?
What quantity are you asking me to estimate?
